questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, what must you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to any traffic close enough to cause a crash.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and keep going without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to any traffic close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: When leaving the interstate, when should you slow down?

options.text: About halfway through the exit lane.
As you get close to the exit lane.
Right when you enter the exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when you enter the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed on the interstate until you enter the exit lane. Then slow down to the speed posted for the exit ramp.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should you turn?

options.text: Into any lane.
Into the first lane.
Into the second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Into the first lane.
questions.explanation: When you turn, always turn from your lane into the first available legal lane. When turning onto a one-way street, turn into the first lane.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, what must you do?

options.text: Let any cars, bikes, or pedestrians in the intersection go first.
Let only pedestrians in the intersection go first.
Wait four seconds before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let any cars, bikes, or pedestrians in the intersection go first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go. Turn in the direction the arrow points after you let any cars, bikes, or pedestrians still in the intersection pass.

questions.question: Why should you stay farther back when driving behind a large vehicle?

options.text: So you can see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pass large vehicles from behind.
Because the large vehicle will pull you along in its air current.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles can block your view of the road. Stay farther back so you can see around them. Also, drivers of trucks, buses, and vans may not see you if you are directly behind them.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beams in fog or mist?

options.text: The light bounces back and blinds you.
Other drivers won't see you.
Vehicles behind you will follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light bounces back and blinds you.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, do not use high beams. The light bounces back off the fog and can blind you.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and move carefully.
Look to the sides of your vehicle to check for oncoming traffic.
Slowly pass vehicles that appear to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to check for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: At any place where people may cross or traffic meets, look left and right to make sure nothing is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Stop.
Warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower.

questions.question: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you should:

options.text: Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and speed up to match traffic.
Use the shoulder of the main road to reach traffic speed.
Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up only after you find a gap in traffic, then enter.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate on a short entrance ramp, find a gap in traffic first. Speed up to match traffic, then enter the lane. Wait while stopped if needed until a safe gap appears.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: For a driver age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 or older cannot legally drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should return to your original lane when:

options.text: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.
You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space to safely pull back in front.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are:

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about traffic laws they must follow. These signs cover speed, parking, turning, direction, and lane use. They are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green symbols.

questions.question: Drivers must use their parking brake:

options.text: Only when parked on an incline.
Only when parked in a parking lot.
Every time they park.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time they park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake when you park. Leave a manual transmission in gear or an automatic transmission in Park.

questions.question: To turn quickly, your hands should be:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and allows you to turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: You should always travel:

options.text: At the speed of vehicles around you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should match road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, you:

options.text: Must stay within your lane.
May cross the centerline to change lanes.
May change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: May cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines between lanes mean lanes travel in the same direction. A broken white line means you may pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, you should NOT:

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: When hit from behind, your body will be thrown backward. Press your head against the head restraint and brace yourself against the back of your seat to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not permitted.
Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Your license will be suspended if you get ____ points within 24 months.

options.text: 15 points
22 points
30 points

questions.correctAnswerText: 22 points
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, getting 22 points or more within 24 months will suspend your license. The length of suspension depends on how many violations you have had.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Broken yellow lines are used to:

options.text: Indicate no passing zones.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean passing is allowed when it is safe.
